pageCache.text:
Brighton
Forward
A specialist Post-16 SEND college, and Alternative Provision, delivering personalised, practical, and supportive learning for young people aged 16 to 25.
Empowering Young People
Supporting vulnerable young people on their journey to independence
Brighton Forward is a specialist post-16 to 25 Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) and Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) college.
We provide a safe, nurturing environment where students build confidence, develop life and work skills, and follow personalised pathways to employability.
We also offer Alternative Provision for Key Stage 4 students, aligned with statutory SEND guidance and the Local Offer.
Our Mission
At Brighton Forward, our mission is to provide meaningful pathways to independence through personalised, practical, and supportive learning experiences.
We are committed to helping young people develop the confidence, communication, resilience, and life skills needed to thrive in adulthood, participate within their communities, and achieve their individual aspirations.
Through nurturing relationships, high expectations, and real-life learning opportunities, we empower every learner to recognise their strengths, make progress from their starting points and prepare positively for their future.
Our Provisions
Main Provision: 3 Post-16 Programmes
Our main provision, Programmes for Post 16, supports young people with SEND and SEMH needs to develop confidence, independence, communication, and practical life skills through personalised learning pathways.
Alternative Provision: KS4
Our alternative provision, Achievability, providing a safe, nurturing and supportive environment for KS4 students who may struggle within mainstream education.
Parent Testimonials
Hear from our community about the impact of Brighton Forward on their lives and futures.
Get in Touch
Have questions about our programmes or admissions? We’d love to hear from you.
info@brightonforward.co.uk

About Us
Brighton Forward is a dedicated Section 41 Specialist College supporting young people aged 16 to 25 with SEND and SEMH needs across Sussex.
Additionally, we provide personalised pathways that support independence and future success, with sites in Worthing and Shoreham.
Safe and Inclusive
Guided by our mission to create meaningful pathways to independence, we provide practical and supportive learning experiences. Furthermore, we help young people prepare for adult life and future opportunities.
Our programmes focus on preparation for adulthood. Students develop life skills, work skills, personal development, and accreditation opportunities through personalised learning. We also provide a nurturing Key Stage 4 Alternative Provision programme. Students rebuild confidence, re-engage with learning, and prepare for education, training, or employment.
Our values of Independence, Respect, Responsibility, Resilience and Communication are at the heart of everything we do. We create a safe and inclusive environment where every learner feels valued and supported.
Learning Beyond the Classroom
Brighton Forward, is a specialist independent post-16 SEND college and alternative provision. We are dedicated to helping young people develop their confidence, independence and practical skills they need for adult life. Additionally, our programmes are designed to support confidence, independence, communication and future aspirations.
We support learners aged 16–25 with a wide range of additional needs through personalised, nurturing and highly practical learning programmes that focus on preparation for adulthood, communication, wellbeing and employability. Through our KS4 alternative provision pathway, Achievability, we also support younger learners who require a more personalised and supportive educational environment.
Our approach is built around strong relationships, high aspirations and meaningful real-life learning. We believe that every young person can make progress when learning is relevant, supportive and tailored to their individual strengths and needs.
At Brighton Forward, learning extends far beyond the classroom. Students take part in practical English and maths, travel training, cooking, community projects, work-related learning, personal development, creative projects and life skills activities designed to promote independence and confidence in everyday life.
Finally, we work closely with families, schools, and professionals to ensure every learner receives personalised support.
Our experienced and caring team creates a safe, inclusive and supportive environment where young people feel valued, understood, and empowered to succeed.
Our Values
Independence
We empower young people to develop the confidence, resilience, and practical skills needed for everyday life, future learning, employment, and greater independence.
Respect
We promote kindness, inclusion, understanding, and positive relationships, ensuring every individual feels safe, valued, listened to and supported within our community.
Responsibility
We encourage young people to take responsibility for their learning, behaviour, choices and personal growth while developing confidence and independence.
Communication
We encourage young people to take responsibility for their learning, behaviour, choices and personal growth while developing confidence and independence.
Resilience
We support learners to build confidence, perseverance, emotional wellbeing and coping strategies that help them overcome challenges and achieve their goals.
How We Can Help
We support young people to build confidence, independence, communication and practical skills for adult life, further education, employment and community participation.
Personalised Support
Individual programmes designed around each learner’s strengths, interests, EHCP outcomes and future goals.
Preparation for Adulthood
Developing independence, communication, confidence, travel training, life skills and employability skills for the future.
Practical Learning
Real-life learning experiences that make English, maths, personal development and work skills meaningful and engaging.
Safe and Nurturing Environment
A supportive and inclusive setting where young people feel safe, respected and able to thrive.
Specialist SEND & Alternative Provision
Support for young people who benefit from smaller group learning, personalised approaches and relationship-based practice.
Working in Partnership
Collaborative support with families, schools, local authorities and professionals to achieve the best outcomes for every learner.
Meet The Team

pageCache.pageTitle: Careers - Brighton Forward | Focus on Careers and Employment
pageCache.text:
Careers
At Brighton Forward, we prioritise equipping our students with the skills and experiences necessary to transition successfully into the workforce.
Our commitment to supporting SEND and vulnerable young people is reflected in our tailored career guidance and work experience programmes, which are designed to align with their individual interests and strengths.
By fostering a secure and supportive environment, we empower our students to explore various career pathways, enhancing their confidence and engagement in the process.
A focus on Careers and Employment
In line with the Gatsby Benchmarks, which provide a framework for good career guidance in schools, we ensure that our students receive comprehensive support across all eight benchmarks.
This includes providing access to a stable careers programme, engaging with employers, and offering meaningful work experience opportunities.
By integrating these benchmarks into our curriculum, we aim to create a seamless transition for our students from education to employment, ultimately setting them on a path toward independence and fulfilling careers.
Our Visits
Visit to Bird & Blend Tea Company
Students met with Meg, Corporate & Community Relationships Manager and Ben, Site Manager of Bird & Blend. Students were told about the company, their ethos, available jobs and then given a tour of the workshop.
They were given a history of tea and got to try numerous types. Meg then challenged the students to complete a questionnaire when they got back to college. The students were fantastic, very engaged and asked so many great questions. What a brilliant visit!
Amy Wayne, Careers Leader
For further information regarding the Careers Programme at Brighton Forward, please contact us.

Safeguarding at Brighton Forward
At Brighton Forward, safeguarding is at the heart of everything we do. We are committed to creating a safe, supportive, respectful and inclusive environment where all young people feel protected, valued, listened to and able to thrive.
Additional Support and Protection
As a Specialist College supporting young people aged 16–25 with SEND and SEMH needs, alongside our Key Stage 4 Alternative Provision pathway, we recognise that many learners may require additional support and protection.
We take our safeguarding responsibilities seriously and work in line with:
Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility, and all staff receive regular safeguarding training to ensure concerns are identified, recorded, and responded to appropriately.
Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE)
Working Together to Safeguard Children
The SEND Code of Practice
Department for Education (DfE) guidance
Alternative Provision guidance
Section 47 safeguarding responsibilities
Local safeguarding partnership procedures
Our Safeguarding Commitment
Brighton Forward is committed to:
We understand that young people with SEND and SEMH needs may experience additional barriers to communication, emotional regulation, relationships, or recognising risks. Therefore, safeguarding support is personalised and responsive to individual needs.
We promote safe and respectful behaviour across all areas of college life and encourage students to speak to trusted adults if they are worried about themselves or others.
Promoting emotional wellbeing, safety, and positive relationships
Creating a culture of vigilance and accountability
Listening to and respecting student voice
Designated Safeguarding Leads (DSL)
Brighton Forward has trained Designated Safeguarding Leads (DSLs) who oversee safeguarding and child protection procedures across the organisation.
The safeguarding team is responsible for:
If a student is at immediate risk of harm, referrals may be made to children’s social care, adult safeguarding, the police, or other relevant agencies in line with statutory safeguarding responsibilities.
Responding to safeguarding concerns
Liaising with local authorities and external agencies
Supporting students and families
Managing referrals and safeguarding records
Providing safeguarding guidance to staff
Safer Recruitment
Brighton Forward follows safer recruitment procedures to help ensure all staff and volunteers are suitable to work with children, young people and vulnerable adults.
All staff receive safeguarding training, including:
Staff receive regular safeguarding updates throughout the year.
